A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MUCAR benchmark and agent framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 19 models, input and language ablations, and agent-framework experiments on MUCAR, CODIS and MMA.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and additionally reports human performance and agreement between GPT-based and human grading.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same ambiguity-detection, evidence-extraction and reasoning stages, including the unified-prompt alternative and equations. Expanded descriptions do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains 1,278 MUCAR queries in 501 groups, seven ambiguity categories and Chinese, English and Malay, alongside CODIS and MMA. The removed appendix descriptions of CODIS and MMA do not remove their evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 adds a quantified human reference across all seven ambiguity categories in Table 2 and Table 9, materially extending the previously model-only comparisons. The 19 evaluated models and the Vanilla, CoT and CODIS prompting comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces reported protocols for human testing with confusing options and GPT–human grading agreement. Section 3.4 also reverses the verbal metric definitions while retaining their equations; this does not establish changed computations or reruns of existing model experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a grading-reliability analysis comparing GPT and human judgments for five models. Existing input-removal and language-prompt ablations remain unchanged. Appendix case changes add translations or alter formatting without changing their findings.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies averaging human scores over three evaluators for Chinese and English and two for Malay. This adds aggregation information, but neither version reports model-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds human overall Accp/Accq of 74.66/86.42 and five grading-agreement scores ranging from 95.26 to 97.57. Retained model-table values are unchanged. Section 4.2 revises numerical summaries: AWQ overall accuracy changes from 67.03 to 63.32, matching Table 2, but its semantics score changes incorrectly from 61.90 to 69.05, the non-AWQ model's value.

T1.justification: V1 describes Accp as requiring all answers in a group to be correct and Accq as individual-query accuracy. V2 reverses these meanings in Section 3.4 while retaining the original product/sum equations, introducing a mathematical inconsistency. The agent equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the multilingual and dual-ambiguity benchmark claims, the human-performance gap and the agent framework's benefits. The new human results support an existing claim rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: V2 adds arguments that grading agreement supports GPT-based evaluation and that carefully curated synthetic images should have negligible effects. It also interprets the retained language-prompt results in greater detail. The original limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code/data access link, annotator backgrounds, eight-curator image selection, image-source proportions and clarification that explanatory notes were withheld during evaluation. Existing inference prompts and model architecture details remain; brief CODIS and MMA dataset descriptions are removed.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged. The Qwen Team citation is updated to Bai et al.'s technical report for the same Qwen2.5-VL work, without introducing a new research comparison.

P1.justification: V2 edits abstract and taxonomy wording, revises section titles, adds ethics and acknowledgment sections, and reorganizes the appendix around dataset details, human evaluation, prompts, models and cases. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the human row and Tables 6–9, and merges v1 Tables 8–11 into Table 12 with unchanged values. Figure 5 receives an expanded caption, Figures 6–7 gain translations, and Figure 13 changes response formatting. The existing figure set is retained.

improvement.justification: V1 claims a human-performance gap without reporting a human baseline; v2 supplies category-level human results and grading-agreement evidence, plus useful access and provenance information. These strengthen support and transparency, but reversed metric definitions and new table-inconsistent summaries limit the net improvement.
